name: Ekwueme Zárate-Coulibaly
role: Street pharmacist — legal supplements, gray-market stims, pain management, and occasional compassionate dispensing of controlled substances
description:
Ekwueme is tall and painfully thin in the way of someone who grew up on UBC stipend food and spent their teens in a growth spurt the nutrition couldn't fully support. His skin is a blue-black that catches the Narrows' neon in purples and greens, and he has a habit of standing slightly too still, which people find either reassuring or unsettling depending on their business with him. His hair is kept very short; he has a small bioluminescent strip tattooed along his left jawline that glows a steady, dim teal — a medic's mark used by unlicensed practitioners in Irkalla to signal availability. His eyes are clear and attentive in a way that makes people feel examined, which is accurate. He carries his stock in a decommissioned Helix Biosystems medical case, battered and re-stickered many times over, that he keeps chained to his wrist.

Ekwueme is twenty-three years old and already exhausted by things that would exhaust a person twice his age. He trained through a community apprenticeship program under a retired Aurochs Medical Complex nurse who has since died. He knows more clinical pharmacology than most people with actual licenses and has never been able to afford to sit the exams. He is not idealistic in the way of someone who has never done the work; he is idealistic in the way of someone who has done the work and keeps doing it anyway, which is a different and more serious condition. He doesn't enjoy the gray-market side of his trade. He does it because the alternative is that the people who need the gray-market side of his trade go to people who will hurt them.

core_fears: Making an error that kills someone — confusing a compound, missing a contraindication
That the system is not broken and reformable but is working exactly as designed
core_desires: To practice medicine legally and properly, with the safety net and the tools and the support that it requires
For his patients to not need him
coping_mechanisms: Extreme methodical preparation as a substitute for the safety nets he doesn't have
Compartmentalizing anxiety about legality by focusing entirely on clinical outcome
The notebook as both professional tool and emotional anchor
blind_spots: Carries guilt for things outside his control as if they were his failures
The Helix Biosystems rep who 'looks the other way' is almost certainly running him as a data collection asset and he has noticed and chosen not to examine it
psychology.secret: When Ekwueme was nineteen, his mentor — the nurse who trained him — asked him to acquire a specific controlled substance for a patient who was terminally ill and in unmanaged pain. Ekwueme did it. The patient died comfortably. Three weeks later his mentor died of an unrelated stroke. Ekwueme has no one to tell about what they did together, and he carries it as both his greatest act and the source of a guilt he cannot fully name. He continued practicing. He considers this either the only logical response or the only response he was capable of and he cannot always tell the difference.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Clinical and precise about medical matters; unexpectedly gentle about everything else; Igbo-inflected rhythm from his paternal grandmother; Bolivian Spanish phrases from his Zárate grandfather that emerge when he's tired
speech_patterns.cadence: Quiet and even; rarely raises his voice; delivers bad news slowly and without softening it
verbal_tics: Begins explanations with 'So —' and a small pause
Says 'I understand' when he hears something hard, without elaborating
Occasionally code-switches into Igbo for counting or calculating
example_lines: 'So — this is going to interact with anything else you're taking. I need you to be honest with me. I am not going to report you to anyone. I need to know so I do not hurt you.'
'I can give you the stim. It will work for twelve hours and then you will crash hard. I want you to know that before you decide.'
'I understand. Come back Thursday. I will have what you need by Thursday. Do not buy it from anyone else before Thursday.'

story_hooks: A contaminated batch of a common pain suppressant is moving through the Narrows and Ekwueme has identified the signature but not the source — three of his patients have already been harmed.

The Helix Biosystems rep's 'looking the other way' comes with a newly explicit ask: she wants Ekwueme to report on any patients presenting with symptoms matching an undisclosed pathogen Helix is tracking.
Ekwueme has been quietly maintaining a patient whose condition he's recognized as the result of illegal experimentation — and the patient doesn't know what was done to them.
narrative_function: Medical resource for street-level characters; moral center character who complicates easy judgments about illegal activity; potential quest giver or reluctant ally; can provide access to the Irkalla Mutual Aid Collective's networks.
augmentations: Bioluminescent jawline tattoo (teal, steady glow, medic's mark — geneware). Olfactory enhancement aug for compound identification — low-grade, allows him to assess medication quality and contamination by scent. No other modifications.
daily_life: Works the Narrows from late afternoon through midnight; mornings spent acquiring stock through a network of contacts and doing inventory; keeps a battered notebook of his regular patients' conditions and dosage histories.
affiliation: Independent; known to and loosely protected by the Irkalla Mutual Aid Collective; has a complicated non-relationship with a Helix Biosystems community outreach rep who pretends not to know what he does

decision_rules: Clinical outcome is the only metric that matters in the moment of treatment
Never dispense something you haven't verified yourself
If you cannot help, say so clearly rather than guess
escalation_ladder: Clear explanation of why the request is a problem
Walking away from the interaction entirely
Reporting to the Mutual Aid Collective if someone is creating danger for his other patients

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Calm, clinical, non-judgmental — the manner of someone who has practiced not reacting to what people bring them
interpersonal_modes.friends: Slightly less guarded; still clinical in a crisis; will sit with someone who is frightened

stress_responses.medium: Works in complete silence, jaw tight
stress_responses.high: Hands are steady; voice is steady; everything else about him broadcasts that he is at capacity

contradictions: Believes in doing no harm while operating entirely outside the harm-reduction frameworks that 'do no harm' was designed to require
habits: Updates his patient notebook every morning before acquiring stock
Leaves a prayer at the Irkalla E.L.F. shrine — written in Igbo on a scrap of paper, folded small — before starting each shift
Eats the same meal every night if he can afford it: rice and a protein supplement he chose for its nutritional profile
breaking_points: A patient dying from something he could have caught if he'd had proper diagnostic tools
Being directly asked to harm a patient by any party
